title: GPU predictive scaling pulse — week of 2027-10-18
content:
Purpose / quick summary:
This note captures the infrastructure standup and engineering pulse focused on the predictive-scaling experiment we ran this week (FleetForecaster v0.3). We tested automated soft-reserves and staggered prewarm triggers across three regions (us-west, eu-west, ap-southeast) to smooth tail latency and reduce on-demand burst cost.

Attendees:
- Sofia Ramirez (owner)
- Ethan Cho
- Priya Nair
- Marco Liu
- Janelle Park
- Ops oncall rotation: team B

Agenda:
1) Quick metrics snapshot
2) Experiment instrumentation & findings
3) Incidents/near-misses
4) Decisions and follow-ups
5) Open questions

Metrics snapshot (week vs baseline):
- Fleet-wide GPU utilization (avg): 68% (baseline 61%) — utilization rose moderately with prewarm enabled, fewer cold-starts observed.
- 95th token latency: 210ms (baseline 260ms) — improvement concentrated in us-west and eu-west.
- Median queue wait: 28ms (baseline 45ms).
- Prewarm-trigger false positives: 4 events (expected ~2) — caused minor warm-only spikes; investigating threshold.
- Estimated marginal cost delta (on-demand vs predictive): -8% token-cost reduction for routed workloads (early estimate from billing simulator).

Experiment overview (FleetForecaster v0.3):
- Model: time-series + calendar + recent-anomaly correction. Trained on 90 days of regional request traces and special events (sales days, model releases).
- Actions: soft-reserve up to N GPUs (configurable per-region) 30–90 minutes before predicted surge; trigger staggered prewarm 15/10/5 minutes prior depending on predicted magnitude.
- Regions tested: us-west (heavy traffic), eu-west (mid), ap-southeast (light; long tail).
- Run mode: canary on 20% of traffic in each region for traffic-tagged routes (internal beta customers).

Key findings and observations:
- Prediction accuracy: 78% of predicted surges (threshold = 12% delta) were within ±10% of observed load. Misses mostly in eu-west where an unannounced customer load happened.
- Latency improvement maps to routes with long context lengths (seq > 1024). Those benefited most from warm KV caches.
- Cost smoothing: predictive prewarming shaved several high-cost on-demand allocations during the daily 09:00–11:00 UTC window in us-west.
- Overprovision risk: ap-southeast saw a 2x over-reserve during a low-confidence prediction; mitigated by fallback auto-drop after 12 minutes, but still resulted in short-lived cost waste.
- Operational complexity: SRE reported that the triage surface increased (more alerts for prediction confidence and reserve failures). Need better alert prioritization.

Incidents / near-misses this week:
- 2027-10-17 10:14 UTC — eu-west spike tied to vendor X integration test. Predictive system flagged low probability; pipeline scaled on demand and recovered in 7 minutes. Root cause: missing customer calendar event in training data. Action: integrate partner release hooks (see action list).
- 2027-10-18 03:02 UTC — prewarm job failed to attach to node due to transient kube-scheduler bug (ticket INF-482). Playbook invoked, fallback to on-demand worked; latency impacted 0.3% of requests in test cohort.

Decisions made:
- Continue FleetForecaster v0.3 canary for two more weeks but tighten safety rules: max soft-reserve per region capped at 15% of baseline pool; auto-drop window reduced to 8 minutes for ap-southeast.
- Add a confidence-weighted mute for predictions flagged as 'low-data' (new label from training pipeline). Low-data predictions will not trigger reserves unless probability > 0.85.
- Prioritize integration of customer release hooks (CI event ingestion) into training dataset — aligns with reducing eu-west misses.

Action items (owner — due):
- Priya Nair — add CI/webhook ingestion for partner releases into FleetForecaster training pipeline (INF-512) — due 2027-10-25.
- Ethan Cho — implement confidence-weighted mute and reduce ap-southeast auto-drop window to 8m; add unit tests for mute logic — due 2027-10-22.
- Marco Liu — dashboard: add prediction-confidence panel and a region-level cost delta estimate for canary cohorts (Confluence doc + grafana) — due 2027-10-21.
- Janelle Park — run a 48-hour cost-simulation across historical spikes with new safety caps and output a short readout (spreadsheet + notes) — due 2027-10-23.
- Sofia Ramirez — update incident playbook with explicit prewarm-attach retry strategy and link to INF-482, coordinate SRE runbook training session — due 2027-10-26.

Notes from SRE / operational team:
- Alerts: currently too many low-severity prediction alerts; propose adding a single summary alert per region per 15m window. Will submit a PR to alerting rules (team: site-reliability-engineering).
- Runbook clarity: “how to force-drop a soft reserve” steps need clearer privileges (only infra-admins), add checklists to avoid accidental force-drops during high traffic.

Open questions / risks:
- How to systematically capture third-party / partner release events in training? Lightweight webhook ingestion is fine but we need a trust model and opt-in from customer teams.
- Is the cost saving consistent across model types (LLama vs Optima variants)? Early signal shows more benefit with larger-context models but the sample size is small.
- Do we want to widen canary to additional private routes? Risk balance vs visibility.

Next steps (this week):
- Execute the action list above; daily quick sync for experiment owners at 10:00 UTC; short update every 48 hours in #infra-fleet.
- SRE and infra to finalize alert tuning PR by EOD 2027-10-20.
- Run a targeted replay of last month’s eu-west spike with and without CI events to measure model sensitivity (data-science + infra joint run).

Appendix: quick checklist for on-call when predictive-reserve triggers
- Verify prediction confidence panel in dashboard (>0.85 recommended).
- Check recent webhook ingestion events for region.
- If prewarm attach fails 3 times in a row, escalate to infra-admin and run the fallback attach script v1.2 (playbook link).
- Post-incident: tag trace with "ff_v0.3_canary" for automatic sampling.

Comments / informal notes:
- Team sentiment: optimistic. Prewarm reduced a lot of the cold-cache spikes we were seeing in the alpha customers; but we need to tighten false-positive handling before a bigger rollout.
- Idea: explore hybrid approach where we warm KV-cache only (cheaper) for low-confidence predictions and full-GPU reserve for high-confidence ones — worth prototyping next sprint.

End of note.
